narrative_purpose: Make tsaheylu legible as a physical neural bridge, not telepathy: two queues' sheaths parted to show the fine living tendrils interlacing like clasped fingers, with signal-light flowing both directions across the join — a cable plugged into a socket, wiring two nervous systems into one.
subject: An intimate close study of two neural queues meeting in mid-air, each sheath gently parted to reveal a bundle of fine pink-and-cyan glowing neural tendrils interlacing like the fingers of two clasped hands; faint pulses of nerve-signal light visibly travelling both ways across the interlaced join.
scene: Held against a deep dark indigo ground with no background detail, so the delicate interlace is the whole subject.
camera: A very close, tender macro view centred on the point where the tendrils interlace, shallow depth into soft dark.
light: Self-luminous tendrils as the only key — pink and cyan bioluminescent glow from the nerve-filaments themselves, faint bloom where signal-pulses cross; deep indigo shadow all around.
palette: Void-indigo ground, biolum magenta-pink and Pandora cyan in the tendrils, a faint living-teal in the signal pulses.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, delicate, hand-painted, intimate.
detail_level: Crisp and fine on the interlacing tendrils and the signal-pulses; everything else soft dark.
composition: The interlace dead-centre with generous dark negative space around it for callout labels, the two queues entering from opposite sides.
consistency_notes: Same glowing-tendril treatment as the tsaheylu glossary cover; reads as living tissue and real synaptic connection, not cables or fibre-optics.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
